    //==
    // # Derived functionality for bounding regions
    //
    // Bodies for the `IBounds<TPoint, TDelta>` interface declared in
    // `intervals-bounds.concepts.plato`, plus the concrete Bounds2D/Bounds3D
    // operations that the generic surface cannot express.
    //
    // Design note on the interface surface: IBounds<TPoint, TDelta> carries a delta
    // type (TDelta = the vector of TPoint, via TPoint: IDifference<TDelta>), so
    // Extent/Diagonal are expressible. Contains/Union/Intersection/Clamp still are
    // not: they need component-wise Min/Max (a ILattice) on TPoint, which the point
    // types do not implement.

    //==
    // IBounds<TPoint, TDelta> — an axis-aligned region between corner points
    // Min and Max, with TDelta the displacement type (TPoint: IDifference<TDelta>).
    // TPoint is declared IDifference<TDelta> and IInterpolatable, so the corner
    // arithmetic below is licensed; it is NOT IOrderable/ILattice.

    // The center point of the region; the MidPoint of the two corners.
    Center(self: IBounds<$TPoint, $TDelta>): $TPoint
        => self.Min.MidPoint(self.Max);
```

    // The angle half way ALONG the arc: Start advanced by half the Span. This is the
    // seam-aware partner of Contains above, and it is deliberately not the generic
    // IInterval.Center (Lerp(0.5), the arithmetic mean of the stored endpoints).
    // The two agree exactly whenever the raw End - Start lies in [0, one turn), which
    // is the regime every arc consumer works in; they diverge only once the stored
    // extent wraps, and there the arithmetic mean is not on the arc at all. For
    // Start = -6.988 rad, End = 2 rad the sweep is Span = 2.705 rad, whose midpoint
    // is -5.636 rad, while the arithmetic mean -2.494 rad sits 4.494 rad along a
    // 2.705 rad arc -- outside the very arc that Span and Contains measure.
    Center(self: AngleInterval): Angle
        => self.Start + self.Span * 0.5;
```
